related_questions.question: What are the 4 stages of pneumonia?

text_blocks.snippet: Pneumonia typically progresses through four stages: congestion, red hepatization, gray hepatization, and resolution. These stages describe the physical changes in the lungs as the infection develops and the body begins to heal.
snippet_highlighted_words: congestion, red hepatization, gray hepatization, and resolution

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of each stage:

list.title: 1. Congestion:
list.snippet: This is the initial stage, occurring within the first 24 hours of infection. The lungs show increased blood flow and swelling in the airways, with some bacteria and white blood cells present. Symptoms include coughing, fatigue, and possible chest pain.

list.title: 2. Red Hepatization:
list.snippet: In this stage, which occurs 2-3 days after the initial infection, the lungs begin to solidify and take on a reddish appearance due to the presence of red blood cells, white blood cells, and fibrin in the air sacs (alveoli). Symptoms may worsen, with increased difficulty breathing and chest pain.

list.title: 3. Gray Hepatization:
list.snippet: This stage develops 4-6 days after infection. The lungs become a grayish color as the red blood cells break down and the lungs become firmer, though still with a liver-like consistency. Symptoms may persist or worsen, with increased difficulty breathing and potential coughing up of blood.

list.title: 4. Resolution:
list.snippet: This final stage marks the beginning of the healing process. The inflammatory fluids and cellular debris in the lungs start to clear, and the airways begin to return to normal. Symptoms gradually improve, and patients start to feel better.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that the progression and duration of these stages can vary depending on the individual and the severity of the pneumonia.
